interactions.description: Only effective when network.type dispatches to LycorisSpecialNetwork; LoRASpecialNetwork ignores this forwarded keyword.

render.description: Enables CP decomposition for eligible non-1x1 LoCon convolution modules.
render.benefits: Can reduce the parameter cost of convolution adaptation.
render.drawbacks: It changes module shape and checkpoint compatibility and applies only to eligible convolutions.

render.description: Selects the concrete adapter architecture variant used by adapter implementations.
render.benefits: Selects the concrete T2I adapter architecture variant constructed for the run.
render.drawbacks: An unsupported variant fails construction or is incompatible with the selected model.

render.description: Sets the channel width at each T2I-adapter stage.
render.benefits: Defines per-stage feature widths so adapter capacity follows the target feature pyramid.
render.drawbacks: Widths that do not match the model produce shape errors and larger widths consume more memory.

render.description: Lists class names used by class-aware adapter workflows.
render.benefits: Supplies an ordered label vocabulary for adapters that consume class-conditioned inputs.
render.drawbacks: Incorrect ordering or names mislabel class-conditioned data.

normalizations.description: When omitted, ip+ selects penultimate_hidden_states and other adapter types select last_hidden_state.

render.description: Selects which CLIP vision representation supplies adapter features.
render.benefits: Chooses which CLIP representation supplies image conditioning to IP-style adapters.
render.drawbacks: The wrong representation can degrade conditioning or mismatch adapter weights.

render.description: Sets the chance that control input is replaced with noise during training.
render.benefits: Regularizes control dependence by replacing a chosen fraction of control images with noise.
render.drawbacks: High dropout weakens control adherence; zero provides no dropout regularization.

render.description: Enables convolutional pooling of adapter embeddings.
render.benefits: Enables a trainable convolutional pooling stage for image-encoder embeddings.
render.drawbacks: Pooling changes embedding shape and must match the adapter implementation.

render.description: Sets the number of convolutional pooling stacks.
render.benefits: Sets the depth of the convolutional pooling stack used for image embeddings.
render.drawbacks: More stacks add capacity, memory use, and training cost.

render.description: Sets the spatial downscale factor used by the adapter.
render.benefits: Aligns adapter spatial reduction with the latent scale expected by the model.
render.drawbacks: A factor inconsistent with model latent resolution causes shape or quality problems.

render.description: Restricts Flux adapter application to double-stream blocks.
render.benefits: Restricts Flux adaptation to double-stream blocks when single-stream coverage is unnecessary.
render.drawbacks: It omits single-stream blocks and can reduce adapter reach.

render.description: Adds the inpainting input channel behavior expected by control adapters.
render.benefits: Declares the additional inpainting input so compatible control adapters accept mask-conditioned channels.
render.drawbacks: Enabling it without matching data/model channels produces incompatible inputs.

render.description: Sets the feature dimension per iLoRA attention head.
render.benefits: Sets the feature width assigned to each iLoRA attention head.
render.drawbacks: Incompatible dimensions cause shape errors; large dimensions cost memory.

render.description: Appends the masked start frame for image-to-video adapter pretraining.
render.benefits: Appends the masked starting frame used by compatible image-to-video adapter pretraining.
render.drawbacks: It changes the expected input layout and is only meaningful for compatible I2V adapters.

render.description: Parses ilora_down into AdapterConfig, but current production code never reads the assigned attribute.
render.benefits: Documents the parsed ilora_down compatibility field and its true default value.
render.drawbacks: Changing ilora_down has no runtime effect because no production path reads the assigned attribute.

render.description: Parses ilora_mid into AdapterConfig, but current production code never reads the assigned attribute.
render.benefits: Documents the parsed ilora_mid compatibility field and its true default value.
render.drawbacks: Changing ilora_mid has no runtime effect because no production path reads the assigned attribute.

render.description: Parses ilora_up into AdapterConfig, but current production code never reads the assigned attribute.
render.benefits: Documents the parsed ilora_up compatibility field and its true default value.
render.drawbacks: Changing ilora_up has no runtime effect because no production path reads the assigned attribute.

render.description: Parses image_dir into AdapterConfig, but current production code never reads the assigned attribute.
render.benefits: Documents the parsed compatibility field for configurations that still contain it.
render.drawbacks: Changing it has no runtime effect because no production path reads the assigned attribute.

render.description: Selects the image-encoder architecture used by the adapter.
render.benefits: Selects the image-encoder implementation that interprets the configured checkpoint.
render.drawbacks: Architecture and checkpoint must agree or loading fails.

render.description: Overrides the image-encoder checkpoint path.
render.benefits: Loads a chosen image-encoder checkpoint instead of relying on an implicit source.
render.drawbacks: A missing or incompatible checkpoint prevents encoder loading.

render.description: Sets adapter input channel count.
render.benefits: Matches the adapter input projection to the channel count of prepared control tensors.
render.drawbacks: It must match prepared control inputs or tensor shapes fail.

render.description: Sets the chance of inverting an inpainting mask during training.
render.benefits: Adds stochastic mask inversion so an inpainting adapter sees both mask orientations.
render.drawbacks: High values change mask semantics frequently and can confuse preservation behavior.

normalizations.description: A present object is parsed through NetworkConfig before use.

render.description: Provides nested network settings for control-LoRA adapters.
render.benefits: Builds the nested NetworkConfig that controls rank and related Control-LoRA behavior.
render.drawbacks: Invalid network settings fail nested NetworkConfig parsing or produce incompatible weights.

interactions.description: This setting is relevant when scaler training is enabled.

render.description: Merges a trained channel scaler into adapter weights on save.
render.benefits: Folds the trained channel scaler into saved adapter weights for simpler deployment.
render.drawbacks: Merged output is harder to resume as a separately trainable scaler.

render.description: Selects an existing adapter name or local path to load.
render.benefits: Initializes the adapter from a named or filesystem checkpoint source.
render.drawbacks: Incompatible weights or a missing path prevent initialization.

render.description: Sets how many model blocks are cloned for LLM adapter training.
render.benefits: Sets how many language-model blocks are cloned for LLM adapter capacity.
render.drawbacks: More cloned blocks sharply increase memory and parameter count.

render.description: Sets the number of control images expected per example.
render.benefits: Configures Control-LoRA to consume the intended number of simultaneous control images.
render.drawbacks: Dataset and model inputs must supply the same count.

render.description: Sets the number of iLoRA attention heads.
render.benefits: Sets the number of attention heads used by the iLoRA adapter.
render.drawbacks: More heads change shapes and increase computation.

render.description: Sets residual blocks per T2I-adapter stage.
render.benefits: Controls residual-block depth and therefore representational capacity in the adapter.
render.drawbacks: More blocks add compute and capacity; checkpoint shapes must match.

normalizations.description: When omitted, type ip+ selects 16 tokens and type ip selects 4 tokens.

render.description: Sets the number of adapter conditioning tokens.
render.benefits: Determines how many learned image-conditioning tokens an IP adapter emits.
render.drawbacks: Token count changes memory and checkpoint shapes and must match the adapter type.

render.description: Caps image size for Pixtral adapter preprocessing.
render.benefits: Caps Pixtral encoder input size to balance retained detail against memory use.
render.drawbacks: Large caps increase encoder memory; small caps discard detail.

render.description: Randomizes Pixtral image size during training.
render.benefits: Introduces input-size variation when preparing images for the Pixtral encoder.
render.drawbacks: It adds scale variation but reduces exact batch-shape predictability.

render.description: Enables four-image composition for applicable vision adapters.
render.benefits: Enables the adapter's quad-image input mode when that implementation supports it.
render.drawbacks: It changes expected inputs and increases image-encoding work.

render.description: Quantizes the LLM used by applicable adapter workflows.
render.benefits: Reduces memory required by the language-model component through quantized loading.
render.drawbacks: Quantization saves memory but can reduce fidelity or add backend constraints.

render.description: Sets SAFE adapter hidden channel width.
render.benefits: Sets the main feature width used by SAFE image-encoder adapter components.
render.drawbacks: Larger widths cost memory and must match saved weights.

render.description: Sets SAFE reducer channel width.
render.benefits: Sets the SAFE reducer width that compresses encoder features before conditioning.
render.drawbacks: An incompatible width causes shape mismatch and larger widths cost memory.

render.description: Sets the number of SAFE adapter tokens.
render.benefits: Sets how many conditioning tokens the SAFE image encoder produces.
render.drawbacks: Token count changes conditioning shape and checkpoint compatibility.

interactions.description: This setting is relevant when scaler training is enabled.

render.description: Overrides learning rate for the trainable adapter scaler.
render.benefits: Tunes the channel scaler with a learning rate independent of other adapter parameters.
render.drawbacks: An excessive scaler rate can destabilize its channel weights.

render.description: Sets sparse-autoencoder feature dimension for applicable adapters.
render.benefits: Chooses the latent width of the optional sparse autoencoder pooling path.
render.drawbacks: Large dimensions increase memory; incompatible dimensions fail shape construction.

render.description: Sets the subpixel adapter downscale factor.
render.benefits: Matches subpixel spatial packing to the scale expected by that adapter architecture.
render.drawbacks: It must match the intended spatial packing or shapes and quality suffer.

normalizations.description: A comma-separated string is split, trimmed, and emptied pieces are discarded.

render.description: Provides one or more fixed test image paths for adapter evaluation.
render.benefits: Provides fixed test images for repeatable adapter evaluation during development.
render.drawbacks: Missing files prevent fixed-image evaluation.

render.description: Selects the adapter text-encoder architecture.
render.benefits: Selects the text-encoder architecture used by adapters with textual conditioning.
render.drawbacks: It must match the configured checkpoint and adapter implementation.

render.description: Overrides the adapter text-encoder checkpoint path.
render.benefits: Loads a specific text-encoder checkpoint for the adapter conditioning path.
render.drawbacks: A missing or incompatible checkpoint prevents loading.

render.description: Enables training of the configured adapter.
render.benefits: Includes adapter parameters in training instead of using the adapter only for conditioning.
render.drawbacks: Leaving it false keeps the adapter out of the trainable adapter path.

render.description: Enables image-encoder parameter training.
render.benefits: Allows the image encoder to adapt its representations to the training dataset.
render.drawbacks: It raises memory use and can overfit a small image set.

normalizations.description: True also forces train_image_encoder true.

interactions.description: This narrows or forces image-encoder training.

render.description: Restricts adapter training to the image encoder.
render.benefits: Focuses optimization on the image encoder while leaving other adapter parameters fixed.
render.drawbacks: It prevents other adapter parameters from learning.

interactions.description: This narrows or forces image-encoder training.

render.description: Restricts image-encoder training to positional embeddings.
render.benefits: Limits image-encoder updates to positional embeddings for a narrowly scoped adaptation.
render.drawbacks: It offers very limited capacity and is only useful for targeted adaptation.

render.description: Enables training of the adapter channel scaler.
render.benefits: Adds a trainable channel scaler that can correct systematic conditioning bias.
render.drawbacks: It adds a separate trainable component that needs an appropriate learning rate.

render.description: Sets the token that activates applicable adapter conditioning.
render.benefits: Defines the trigger token used to associate prompts with adapter conditioning.
render.drawbacks: A common or inconsistent trigger can entangle adapter behavior.

render.description: Sets the class name associated with the adapter trigger for masked-prior workflows.
render.benefits: Names the semantic class used when constructing preservation-aware adapter prompts.
render.drawbacks: An incorrect class name gives the preservation target the wrong semantics.

render.description: Selects the top-level adapter family.
render.benefits: Dispatches construction to the intended adapter family, such as IP or Control-LoRA.
render.drawbacks: Each family requires different inputs, weights, and compatible model support.

render.description: Sets the square resolution used to cache and compare validation latents.
render.benefits: Makes resolution explicit for repeatable validation checks.
render.drawbacks: Higher resolution increases validation memory and time and must suit the model.

render.description: Sets the optimizer-step interval between validation loss evaluations.
render.benefits: Makes validate every n steps explicit for repeatable validation checks.
render.drawbacks: Short intervals add repeated validation work and slow training.

normalizations.description: Mapping items are converted to ValidationItem objects; existing ValidationItem objects are retained.

render.description: Lists fixed images and prompts used for validation.
render.benefits: Makes validation items explicit for repeatable validation checks.
render.drawbacks: Missing or invalid image items are skipped, and an empty usable list disables validation.

render.description: Lists noise sigma levels evaluated for each validation item.
render.benefits: Makes validation sigmas explicit for repeatable validation checks.
render.drawbacks: More sigma levels multiply validation work; unsuitable levels may not represent the training regime.

render.description: Points to the fixed image encoded for one validation case.
render.benefits: Makes each validation item's image path explicit and repeatable.
render.drawbacks: An empty or missing path causes the item to be skipped.

render.description: Sets the prompt paired with this validation image.
render.benefits: Makes each validation item's prompt explicit and repeatable.
render.drawbacks: A prompt unrelated to the image makes the validation loss harder to interpret.

render.description: Sets the source text used to initialize new embedding token vectors.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of embedding init words.
render.drawbacks: Poor initialization can slow convergence or bias the learned token toward an unrelated concept.

render.description: Chooses safetensors or PyTorch serialization for the learned embedding.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of embedding save format.
render.drawbacks: PyTorch and safetensors outputs target different consumers and have different safety properties.

render.description: Sets the number of trainable tokens allocated to the embedding.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of embedding tokens.
render.drawbacks: More tokens add capacity but make prompting and optimization more complex.

render.description: Sets the prompt trigger that expands to the learned embedding tokens.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of embedding trigger.
render.drawbacks: A common trigger can collide with existing vocabulary and entangle the concept.

interactions.description: The class name supplies the preservation class associated with the trigger.

render.description: Sets the class name used with the embedding trigger for inverted masked-prior behavior.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of embedding trigger class name.
render.drawbacks: An incorrect class name gives preservation prompts the wrong semantic target.

render.description: Sets the number of trainable decorator tokens created for a supported Flux process.
render.benefits: Controls decorator representation capacity.
render.drawbacks: More tokens increase trainable state and prompt complexity; decorator configuration is rejected for non-Flux models.

interactions.description: This setting is effective only when EMA is enabled.

render.description: Sets exponential moving-average decay for shadow parameters.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of EMA ema decay.
render.drawbacks: High decay responds slowly; low decay follows noisy current weights too closely.

interactions.description: This setting is effective only when EMA is enabled.

render.description: Multiplies live parameters after every EMA update.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of EMA param multiplier.
render.drawbacks: Values other than one directly grow or shrink live weights and can destabilize training.

normalizations.description: TrainConfig replaces the entire EMA object with {use_ema: false} unless the input object explicitly enables EMA.

render.description: Enables creation and updates of exponential moving-average shadow weights.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of EMA use ema.
render.drawbacks: EMA consumes an additional copy of trainable parameters and update time.

interactions.description: This setting is effective only when EMA is enabled.

render.description: Feeds a scaled EMA difference back into live parameters.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of EMA use feedback.
render.drawbacks: Feedback changes optimization dynamics and can destabilize an otherwise tuned run.

render.description: Sets the scale stored for the optional process guidance configuration.
render.benefits: Preserves the guidance scale field for compatibility with guidance-aware extensions.
render.drawbacks: The current core trainer parses but does not consume this guidance object, so changing it has no runtime effect.

render.description: Stores the negative prompt for optional training guidance.
render.benefits: Preserves the negative prompt field for compatibility with guidance-aware extensions.
render.drawbacks: The current core trainer parses but does not consume this guidance object.

render.description: Stores the positive prompt for optional training guidance.
render.benefits: Preserves the positive prompt field for compatibility with guidance-aware extensions.
render.drawbacks: The current core trainer parses but does not consume this guidance object.

render.description: Stores the target class for optional training guidance.
render.benefits: Preserves the target class field for compatibility with guidance-aware extensions.
render.drawbacks: The current core trainer parses but does not consume this guidance object.

render.description: Selects the diffusion noise schedule used to add training noise.
render.benefits: Using the schedule expected by the base model keeps timestep and target calculations aligned.
render.drawbacks: A mismatched schedule risks training against a noise process the base model was not designed to reverse.

interactions.description: Content/style bias is used after specialized timestep modes, so those modes can take precedence.

render.description: Biases timestep sampling toward content, style, or a balanced distribution.
render.benefits: Use content or style weighting when the concept benefits from emphasis on structure or appearance.
render.drawbacks: Strong weighting risks weakening learning in the other part of the denoising trajectory.

interactions.description: The loop runs from the effective starting counter toward train.steps, so resumed counters reduce remaining iterations.

render.description: Sets the target number of optimizer steps for the run.
render.benefits: Use a larger step budget when the dataset and validation samples still improve without overfitting.
render.drawbacks: Long schedules risk overfitting and resume behavior depends on the saved step counter.

render.description: Sets the global learning rate inherited by components without an override.
render.benefits: Use 1e-4 as an assertive starting example when rapid adapter learning is more important than conservatism.
render.drawbacks: A high global rate risks unstable updates or fast overfitting, so validate samples early.

normalizations.description: Omission inherits train.lr; explicit null is preserved and is not a numeric learning rate.

render.description: Overrides the learning rate for the denoising network.
render.benefits: Use 5e-5 for a moderate denoiser update that is gentler than an aggressive global rate.
render.drawbacks: A denoiser-specific override risks diverging from the text or adapter components if rates are poorly balanced.

normalizations.description: Omission inherits train.lr; explicit null is preserved and is not a numeric learning rate.

render.description: Overrides the learning rate for trainable text encoders.
render.benefits: Use 2e-5 when prompt-language adaptation is needed but should move more cautiously than the denoiser.
render.drawbacks: Text encoders are sensitive; a larger rate risks damaging general prompt understanding.

normalizations.description: Omission inherits train.lr; explicit null is preserved and is not a numeric learning rate.

render.description: Overrides the learning rate for a trainable refiner component.
render.benefits: Use 1e-5 for slow refinement updates when preserving the pretrained refiner is important.
render.drawbacks: A very small rate risks negligible change, while a larger one can over-specialize the refiner.

normalizations.description: Omission inherits train.lr; explicit null is preserved and is not a numeric learning rate.

render.description: Overrides the learning rate for trained embedding parameters.
render.benefits: Use 1e-5 when an embedding should learn steadily without outrunning the surrounding network.
render.drawbacks: An embedding rate that is too high risks collapsing token meaning into a narrow dataset pattern.

normalizations.description: Omission inherits train.lr; explicit null is preserved and is not a numeric learning rate.

render.description: Overrides the learning rate for the optional adapter component.
render.benefits: Use 5e-6 for conservative adapter tuning when its pretrained behavior should mostly be retained.
render.drawbacks: A low rate risks under-training the adapter, while an excessive rate can erase useful conditioning behavior.

render.description: Selects the learning-rate scheduler dispatched by the toolkit.
render.benefits: Use a constant schedule when a fixed rate is easier to reason about across short fine-tuning runs.
render.drawbacks: An unsuitable scheduler risks decaying too soon or applying warmup parameters that do not fit the run length.

interactions.description: These keyword arguments are interpreted only by the selected learning-rate scheduler.

render.description: Passes scheduler-specific keyword arguments to learning-rate scheduler dispatch.
render.benefits: Use total_iters to align compatible cosine schedules with the intended training duration.
render.drawbacks: Unsupported keys risk constructor errors, and constant_with_warmup removes total_iters before dispatch.

interactions.description: The lower timestep bound must not exceed the effective upper bound.

render.description: Sets the lowest denoising-step index eligible for sampled training timesteps.
render.benefits: Use a higher floor to focus learning away from the cleanest end of the trajectory.
render.drawbacks: A restrictive floor risks leaving low-noise behavior under-trained.

interactions.description: The upper timestep bound is paired with the configured lower bound.

render.description: Sets the highest denoising-step index eligible for sampled training timesteps.
render.benefits: Use a lower ceiling to avoid the noisiest part of a scheduler when a recipe calls for that focus.
render.drawbacks: A low ceiling risks weakening generation from heavily noised latents.

interactions.description: Effective batch size grows with both the micro-batch size and accumulated micro-batches.

render.description: Sets the number of dataset items processed together in each micro-batch.
render.benefits: Use a larger batch when memory permits and a smoother per-step gradient estimate is useful.
render.drawbacks: Larger batches risk out-of-memory failures and change the effective batch with accumulation.

render.description: Enables minimum-SNR loss weighting when set to a positive number.
render.benefits: Use a positive gamma to reduce domination by timesteps with extreme signal-to-noise ratios.
render.drawbacks: Poorly chosen weighting risks suppressing useful gradients from parts of the trajectory.

render.description: Enables SNR-based loss weighting with the configured gamma.
render.benefits: Use SNR weighting when balancing timestep contributions is more useful than uniform loss.
render.drawbacks: An aggressive gamma risks shifting learning away from timesteps important to the target model.

render.description: Enables learned gamma, offset, and scale terms for timestep loss balancing.
render.benefits: Use the learned adjustment only for experiments that need adaptive weighting across timesteps.
render.drawbacks: The experimental adjustment risks harder-to-diagnose loss dynamics than fixed weighting.

render.description: Controls random jitter applied to supported training weights.
render.benefits: Use a small nonzero jitter only when the active trainer consumes it as deliberate regularization.
render.drawbacks: Jitter risks adding variance and some trainer paths do not consume this parsed value.

interactions.description: start_step changes the initial counter used by the loop and must remain meaningful relative to the target step count.

render.description: Overrides the initial step counter before the training loop starts.
render.benefits: Use start_step when deliberately resuming step-sensitive scheduling from a known counter.
render.drawbacks: A mismatched counter risks skipped work, shifted sampling, and scheduler state that disagrees with checkpoints.

render.description: Sets the training timestep domain used by supported flow and weighting paths.
render.benefits: Use the base model's expected timestep count so sampled indices and scheduler scaling agree.
render.drawbacks: A mismatched count risks incorrect timestep normalization and out-of-range assumptions.

interactions.description: The legacy interval must remain 1 when the current accumulation setting exceeds 1.

render.description: Sets the legacy optimizer-step interval, with -1 accumulating for an entire epoch.
render.benefits: Use 1 for ordinary stepping or -1 only for a deliberately small epoch-sized accumulation.
render.drawbacks: Large or epoch-wide accumulation risks high memory use and conflicts with gradient_accumulation above 1.

interactions.description: TrainConfig raises when gradient_accumulation exceeds 1 while gradient_accumulation_steps is not 1.

render.description: Sets the number of micro-batches accumulated for each visible training step.
render.benefits: Use accumulation to increase effective batch size when a full batch does not fit in memory.
render.drawbacks: More accumulation risks slower feedback and cannot be combined with a nondefault legacy interval; fused-backward optimizers update during each backward call instead of waiting for this outer accumulation loop.

render.description: Forces supported batching tricks to process one item at a time while accumulating gradients.
render.benefits: Use single-item batching when a training method expands a logical batch but needs isolated forwards.
render.drawbacks: Serializing items risks lower throughput and still accumulates their gradients before the update.

render.description: Scales loss from regularization images relative to ordinary training images.
render.benefits: Use a lower or higher multiplier to tune how strongly prior-preservation examples affect updates.
render.drawbacks: Excessive regularization weight risks under-learning the target concept; too little risks forgetting.

render.description: Selects the supported timestep sampling strategy.
render.benefits: Use sigmoid for the engine fallback or a model-compatible specialized strategy for deliberate trajectory emphasis.
render.drawbacks: An unsupported or model-incompatible strategy risks a runtime ValueError or poorly distributed training noise.

interactions.description: This count is consumed when timestep_type selects next_sample.

render.description: Sets the shortened timestep count used by next-sample training.
render.benefits: Use a small count when timestep_type is next_sample and the recipe needs a short denoising path.
render.drawbacks: Too few timesteps risk coarse targets; the value has no effect outside next-sample handling.

interactions.description: The legacy flag also makes guidance paths treat timestep weighting as linear.

render.description: Enables the first legacy linear-timestep weighting table.
render.benefits: Use it only with scheduler paths that expose the matching precomputed weights.
render.drawbacks: Enabling legacy weighting risks unexpected emphasis and overlaps with timestep_type linear.

interactions.description: The alternate legacy flag also makes guidance paths treat timestep weighting as linear.

render.description: Enables the second legacy linear-timestep weighting table.
render.benefits: Use it only when the selected scheduler provides the alternate weighting table.
render.drawbacks: The alternate legacy curve risks unintended timestep bias and is not universal across schedulers.

render.description: Sets how often multi-stage training switches the active model boundary.
render.benefits: Use 1 to alternate at every supported boundary opportunity or a larger interval for longer stage runs.
render.drawbacks: A long interval risks imbalanced stage updates; the setting is inert for single-stage models.

render.description: Lets supported loaders adapt latent scaling from observed image norms.
render.benefits: Can compensate when encoded magnitudes differ from the model's expected scale.
render.drawbacks: Adaptive scaling changes input statistics and can make runs harder to compare.

render.description: Scales the audio loss contribution in audio-capable training.
render.benefits: Balances audio supervision against other loss terms in multimodal batches.
render.drawbacks: A large multiplier can let audio dominate the shared update.

render.description: Sets the strength of noise borrowed from other items for batch correction.
render.benefits: Can discourage the model from drifting toward unrelated examples in the same batch.
render.drawbacks: Strong correction adds cross-example interference and depends on meaningful batches.

interactions.description: Configuration validation rejects enabling both preservation modes.

render.description: Adds a preservation target generated from an empty prompt.
render.benefits: Helps retain the base model's unconditional behavior while a network learns a concept.
render.drawbacks: It requires a network and cannot run with differential output preservation.

interactions.description: The multiplier is consumed only when blank-prompt preservation supplies the active target.

render.description: Scales the blank-prompt preservation loss.
render.benefits: Allows preservation strength to be balanced against the main objective.
render.drawbacks: Too much preservation can suppress learning of the requested concept.

render.description: Blends blurred structure into generated training noise.
render.benefits: Can expose the denoiser to a structured-noise variant for targeted experiments.
render.drawbacks: The altered noise distribution may not match the base model's training process.

normalizations.description: Omission or explicit null is replaced with cfg_scale.

interactions.description: Omission is normalized to cfg_scale before training uses the value.

render.description: Sets the CFG rescale used during CFG-enabled training targets.
render.benefits: Separates guidance amplitude correction from the primary CFG scale.
render.drawbacks: Omission falls back to cfg_scale, while an ill-chosen value can distort targets.

render.description: Sets the base classifier-free guidance scale used by training paths.
render.benefits: Provides direct control over conditional extrapolation when CFG training is enabled.
render.drawbacks: High guidance can amplify prediction errors and destabilize targets.

render.description: Corrects target statistics using the prediction mean and standard deviation.
render.benefits: Can counter prediction-norm drift when a prior prediction is available.
render.drawbacks: The extra prior pass and normalization can increase cost and alter loss geometry.

render.description: Scales prediction-norm correction before it is applied.
render.benefits: Allows the norm correction to be introduced gently.
render.drawbacks: Large multipliers can overcorrect and replace useful target variation.

interactions.description: Configuration validation rejects enabling both preservation modes.
SDTrainer rejects differential output preservation while text encoders are trained.

render.description: Preserves the network-off output for a prompt with the trigger removed.
render.benefits: Helps a LoRA learn the trigger-specific difference instead of rewriting the whole class.
render.drawbacks: It requires a trigger and network, conflicts with text-encoder training, and excludes blank preservation.

render.description: Replaces the trigger with a class phrase for differential preservation.
render.benefits: Provides a stable class prompt when the trigger should be removed from the reference pass.
render.drawbacks: A poor replacement class teaches preservation against the wrong semantic baseline.

interactions.description: The multiplier is consumed only when differential preservation supplies the active preservation target.

render.description: Scales the differential-output preservation loss.
render.benefits: Balances class preservation against trigger-specific learning.
render.drawbacks: Excessive weight can prevent the network from making the desired change.

interactions.description: The scale is consumed by the differential-guidance path.

render.description: Sets the extrapolation scale for differential guidance loss.
render.benefits: Controls how strongly the guided difference contributes to training.
render.drawbacks: Large extrapolation magnifies noisy differences and can destabilize loss.

interactions.description: Disabling sampling subsumes the first-sample skip.
Disabling sampling prevents even a forced first sample.

render.description: Disables first, periodic, and final sample generation for the run.
render.benefits: Saves generation time and memory in runs evaluated by other means.
render.drawbacks: Removing samples makes qualitative regressions harder to catch during training.

render.description: Enables batch-derived noise correction.
render.benefits: Can push each item away from features represented by its batch neighbors.
render.drawbacks: It adds a batch-dependent signal and has little meaning for isolated items.

render.description: Enables zero-prediction stabilization for empty prompts.
render.benefits: Can reduce unwanted output from unconditional text conditioning.
render.drawbacks: The extra objective may weaken useful unconditional behavior if overemphasized.

render.description: Enables classifier-free-guidance construction during training.
render.benefits: Can train against conditional and unconditional predictions explicitly.
render.drawbacks: CFG training adds model work and depends on compatible prompt handling.

interactions.description: The scale controls the differential-guidance extrapolation.

render.description: Enables the differential-guidance objective.
render.benefits: Can emphasize the change produced by guidance instead of only absolute prediction error.
render.drawbacks: The additional extrapolated target can be noisy and is architecture-sensitive.

render.description: Adds a frequency-domain loss term.
render.benefits: Can emphasize frequency structure that pixel losses underweight.
render.drawbacks: FFT loss increases computation and may over-prioritize texture frequencies.

render.description: Applies velocity-equivalent weighting to the FFT objective.
render.benefits: Can align frequency loss weighting with velocity-style timestep behavior.
render.drawbacks: Combining specialized weights makes the effective objective harder to interpret.

interactions.description: The target supplies the guidance value used by the auxiliary loss.
The schedule controls whether that target stays constant or decays with sigma.
Configuration validation rejects guidance loss while guidance embedding is bypassed.

render.description: Enables a guidance-distillation loss toward a configured target.
render.benefits: Supports models that need explicit guidance behavior during fine-tuning.
render.drawbacks: It conflicts with bypassed guidance embeddings and adds another coupled objective.

render.description: Uses zero CFG conditioning for the guidance-loss auxiliary pass.
render.benefits: Can isolate guidance behavior from a nonzero CFG baseline.
render.drawbacks: Zero conditioning may be inappropriate for models trained around a fixed guidance value.

render.description: Applies negative prior loss to encourage divergence from the base prediction.
render.benefits: Can deliberately push a concept away from its pretrained prior.
render.drawbacks: Negative loss can erase useful prior knowledge or produce unstable gradients.

interactions.description: Random CFG needs the configured maximum to define its scale range.

render.description: Randomizes CFG scale within the configured range.
render.benefits: Exposes the model to more than one guidance strength.
render.drawbacks: Random guidance adds target variance and depends on a sensible maximum scale.

render.description: Amplifies selected training signal before target construction.
render.benefits: Can strengthen a weak target signal in experimental recipes.
render.drawbacks: Amplification also magnifies noise and can destabilize updates.

render.description: Adds signal-correction noise during noising.
render.benefits: Can compensate for signal leakage in selected training setups.
render.drawbacks: The corrected distribution differs from ordinary scheduler noise.

render.description: Selects the tensor dtype used by training components.
render.benefits: Lower precision can reduce memory use and increase accelerator throughput.
render.drawbacks: Low precision can overflow or lose small updates, and float8 needs hardware and kernels that support it.

render.description: Makes noise offset vary dynamically instead of remaining fixed.
render.benefits: Can diversify offset exposure across training examples.
render.drawbacks: Dynamic offsets add variance and reduce reproducibility of the target distribution.

normalizations.description: Omission or null becomes an EMAConfig with use_ema false; an object with use_ema true is normalized before construction.

render.description: Configures the exponential moving average of trained parameters.
render.benefits: EMA can provide a smoother parameter snapshot for saving or evaluation.
render.drawbacks: It consumes additional memory and a slow decay can lag rapid learning.

render.description: Reuses consistent noise for the same image and size.
render.benefits: Reduces noise variation when comparing repeated presentations of an example.
render.drawbacks: Less noise diversity can encourage memorization of image-specific trajectories.

interactions.description: disable_sampling takes precedence and prevents the forced first sample.

render.description: Forces initial sample generation even when ordinary first-sample logic would skip it.
render.benefits: Provides a baseline sample at the start of a run.
render.drawbacks: The extra generation delays training and disable_sampling still takes precedence.

render.description: Recomputes supported module activations during backward to save memory.
render.benefits: Enables larger models or resolutions within the same VRAM budget.
render.drawbacks: Backward becomes slower and only components exposing checkpoint support are affected.

interactions.description: The schedule affects training only while guidance loss is enabled.

render.description: Chooses constant or sigma-decayed guidance-loss targeting.
render.benefits: Sigma decay reduces extrapolation as fresh-noise influence becomes less predictable.
render.drawbacks: A schedule that does not match the model's guidance behavior can misweight timesteps.

normalizations.description: A tuple guidance target is converted to a list after parsing.

interactions.description: The target affects training only while guidance loss is enabled.

render.description: Sets the guidance target, optionally supplied as a list before normalization.
render.benefits: Controls the endpoint used by the auxiliary guidance objective.
render.drawbacks: An aggressive target can amplify unstable conditional differences.

render.description: Scales image tensors before supported latent preparation.
render.benefits: Can correct known input scaling differences in specialized pipelines.
render.drawbacks: Changing image magnitude can invalidate model normalization assumptions.

interactions.description: The multiplier directly scales the prior loss outside the active mask.
SDTrainer asserts that Turbo training is disabled when it computes the inverted-mask prior.

render.description: Uses the network-off prediction as an unmasked-region prior target.
render.benefits: Preserves areas outside a dataset mask while the masked concept changes.
render.drawbacks: It requires masks and a prior prediction, and Turbo training triggers source assertions.

interactions.description: The multiplier is used only when an inverted-mask prior prediction and mask are available.

render.description: Scales loss from the inverted-mask prior region.
render.benefits: Balances unmasked preservation against learning inside the mask.
render.drawbacks: A large value can dominate the main masked objective.

render.description: Scales clean latents used by supported training paths.
render.benefits: Can match a specialized model's latent magnitude convention.
render.drawbacks: Incorrect scaling changes both noising and target magnitudes.

render.description: Selects which prediction target the loss compares against.
render.benefits: Supports noise prediction and source-oriented objectives used by specialized recipes.
render.drawbacks: A target incompatible with the scheduler or model prediction type produces misleading gradients.

render.description: Selects MSE or a recognized alternate loss calculation.
render.benefits: MAE, pseudo-Huber, wavelet, stepped, and mean-flow paths allow task-specific error shaping.
render.drawbacks: Unrecognized spellings fall through ordinary MSE paths instead of selecting a new loss.

render.description: Matches sampled noise norm before loss construction.
render.benefits: Can retain the model's learned brightness or magnitude distribution.
render.drawbacks: Norm matching removes natural variation and can bias the noise statistics.

normalizations.description: Omission inherits cfg_scale; explicit null is preserved and is not a numeric upper bound.

interactions.description: Random CFG draws use cfg_scale as the lower endpoint and max_cfg_scale as the upper endpoint.

render.description: Sets the upper CFG scale used when random CFG is enabled.
render.benefits: Bounds random guidance to a deliberate range.
render.drawbacks: A maximum below cfg_scale or an excessive ceiling makes randomization unhelpful or unstable.

render.description: Clips ordinary optimizer gradients to the configured norm.
render.benefits: Limits unusually large updates before non-fused optimizer steps.
render.drawbacks: Fused-backward optimizers update inside backward before this clipping point, so the limit cannot constrain those updates.

render.description: Clips supported per-step loss values at a maximum.
render.benefits: Can keep rare extreme losses from dominating an update.
render.drawbacks: Clipping can hide data or numerical failures and changes the objective above the cap.

render.description: Enables detailed diagnostics when loss exceeds the configured maximum.
render.benefits: Helps trace examples that create extreme loss values.
render.drawbacks: Additional diagnostics can be noisy and do not fix the underlying instability.

render.description: Limits how many negative prompts are retained for supported CFG paths.
render.benefits: Bounds negative-conditioning work and memory.
render.drawbacks: Too few negatives reduce variety; extra entries add encoding cost.

render.description: Scales the primary sampled noise.
render.benefits: Allows deliberate adjustment of noising strength in specialized recipes.
render.drawbacks: Departing from scheduler scale changes the training distribution.

render.description: Adds an offset component to sampled training noise.
render.benefits: Can improve learning of very bright or dark image distributions.
render.drawbacks: Large offsets bias the model away from the scheduler's original noise process.

render.description: Scales latents after noise is applied.
render.benefits: Can match specialized model input magnitude conventions.
render.drawbacks: The multiplier alters the denoiser input without changing the nominal timestep.

render.description: Sets the candidate count for optimal noise pairing.
render.benefits: Multiple candidates can choose noise better matched to an image under the pairing heuristic.
render.drawbacks: More candidates increase preparation cost and can reduce stochastic diversity.

render.description: Scales model predictions before selected loss calculations.
render.benefits: Can tune detail emphasis in experimental objectives.
render.drawbacks: Prediction scaling changes loss magnitude and can require learning-rate retuning.

render.description: Sets the probability of dropping text before encoding.
render.benefits: Builds robustness to missing conditioning and supplies unconditional examples.
render.drawbacks: Too much dropout weakens prompt alignment.

render.description: Sets the chance of repeating a prompt to saturate the encoder.
render.benefits: Can test stronger text-encoder activation for prompt-sensitive concepts.
render.drawbacks: Repeated text may create unnatural conditioning and token truncation.

render.description: Adds random variation to the noise multiplier.
render.benefits: Broadens the noising strengths seen during training.
render.drawbacks: Extra randomness makes targets less reproducible and can exceed useful scale.

render.description: Randomly shifts sampled noise values.
render.benefits: Can diversify offset-like perturbations across batches.
render.drawbacks: Large shifts bias the noise mean and destabilize scheduler assumptions.

interactions.description: Raw Turbo output display is reached only in Turbo sampling.

render.description: Shows raw Turbo outputs in the sampling path.
render.benefits: Makes Turbo-specific behavior visible during qualitative evaluation.
render.drawbacks: It has no training effect without train_turbo and adds sample work.

render.description: Sets the strength used when signal amplification is enabled.
render.benefits: Allows the experimental signal boost to be tuned gradually.
render.drawbacks: High strength magnifies artifacts along with useful signal.

render.description: Scales the correction-noise term.
render.benefits: Controls how much signal correction changes the sampled noise.
render.drawbacks: Large values can overwhelm the scheduler noise.

interactions.description: skip_first_sample is checked before force_first_sample in initial sampling logic.

render.description: Skips automatic sample generation at the first training step.
render.benefits: Starts optimization sooner when a baseline sample is unnecessary.
render.drawbacks: Without an initial sample there is no direct visual before-and-after reference.

render.description: Standardizes image inputs to reference mean and variance.
render.benefits: Can align atypical datasets with expected input statistics.
render.drawbacks: Standardization changes colors and contrast when the model did not expect it.

render.description: Standardizes encoded latents before training.
render.benefits: Can compensate for latent statistics that differ from the model baseline.
render.drawbacks: It changes the latent distribution and may conflict with fixed VAE scaling.

render.description: Adds a target based on prediction at timestep zero.
render.benefits: Can directly supervise the fully denoised endpoint.
render.drawbacks: The extra target increases compute and may compete with the sampled-timestep objective.

render.description: Applies velocity-equivalent weighting to the timestep-zero loss.
render.benefits: Can align the endpoint objective with velocity prediction scaling.
render.drawbacks: Specialized weighting complicates comparison with ordinary t0 loss.

render.description: Scales noise used in target construction independently of input noise.
render.benefits: Allows experimental target magnitude adjustment.
render.drawbacks: Different input and target scales can create inconsistent denoising supervision.

render.description: Enables target standard-deviation correction when set.
render.benefits: Can encourage predictions toward a chosen output spread.
render.drawbacks: Forcing a target spread can remove useful variation or destabilize normalization.

interactions.description: The target value is used when target standard-deviation correction is enabled.

render.description: Sets the desired standard deviation for target-norm correction.
render.benefits: Provides the numeric endpoint used by the correction path.
render.drawbacks: A mismatched value biases output contrast or magnitude.

render.description: Sets the unconditional text used by guidance loss.
render.benefits: Allows guidance training to use a deliberate negative or empty baseline.
render.drawbacks: A semantically loaded baseline changes what the guidance difference means.
